items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: Well, his name was Barry Astuart. He played second horn in that orchestra.

ctx.x: I've heard of one clarinetist, I think, by that name. No, no, not that. No, no, no. I don't know.

I don't think you heard of them. Because the last one died, the youngest daughter, she was an accomplished pianist. No, I never knew. They had a brother that was a tromborist and a French horn. Well, that's the one of them. Well, his name was Barry Astuart. He played second horn in that orchestra. But Jean-Jacques played first horn. And we're talking about a man that had a lips that did. He'd never come to. It was once said that a person with a thick lips couldn't play a trumpet. They'd have to have thin lips.…
The real old musicians were all gone. Much like most of them are gone. All gone. Kiku is about one of the old. And then Kiku.
